purpose.domain_detail: Textbook exercise implementing array algorithms from 'Essential Algorithms' by Rod Stephens
purpose.summary: This program builds a one-dimensional integer array from user input, then performs linear search for a target value, finds minimum/maximum/average, and inserts a value at a specified position. It is a direct implementation of array algorithm exercises from a programming textbook.

notable_features: ALLOCATE with LOC 31 (Micro Focus/Visual COBOL extension)
USAGE IS POINTER with VALUE IS NULL
OCCURS without DEPENDING ON used with dynamic allocation
No IDENTIFICATION or ENVIRONMENT divisions present
Typos in display strings ('Emter amy key')
verdict.notes: Missing IDENTIFICATION DIVISION and ENVIRONMENT DIVISION; the AS clause in PROGRAM-ID and ALLOCATE LOC 31 strongly suggest Micro Focus Visual COBOL targeting .NET. The comment references 'Essential Algorithms' by Rod Stephens, confirming this is a student/learning exercise. Several typos ('Emter amy key to continue') suggest informal/student authorship. The ALLOCATE/pointer logic appears partially implemented and may not be fully functional.
